 Star Exclusive VIP Monday musings: October 19 
 Back home; Tre White reflects on his return to Allen Fieldhouse
 The super senior felt the same energy and crowd pop despite a new team and new faces. 
 Jack Ritter VIP 0 With 14:42 left in the first half of Kansas basketball's 80-62 exhibition win over Pitt State, Tre White was standing on the edge of the Big 12 Monster Energy logo in the paint on defense. Seconds later, he'd be on the complete other end and scoring for the first time in Allen Fieldhouse since senior day on March 7.
 Tyran Stokes grabbed a defensive rebound that came off the back iron and whipped around, looking to push the ball. Stokes found Taylen Kinney , who was about a third up the court on the far sideline. Kinney came slashing down the court at a diagonal angle, cutting in between White and two Pitt State defenders.
 The slash set up White perfectly for a perimeter 3 attempt, so Kinney dumped the ball off to the fifth-year senior. With no hesitation, White put up on a shot with a Gorilla defender in his face. Nothing but net. The 3 rang home, and so would White's next two attempts from deep. The super senior made his first three attempts and finished 4-for-7 shooting from deep in the win.
 After making the deep shot, White gestured to the crowd with both hands in the air, almost as if to say, "I'm back home."
 "Just got that monkey off my back," White said. "I didn't know if it was going to be a layup, a free throw, or whatever it was going to be. But I'm grateful to be back in there and feeling that energy for sure. Even though it was an exhibition game preseason, we still felt the energy."
